reason: It fails the feasibility/schedule check as an LB mechanism, although the code itself is buildable. (1) Buildable: an env flag (default 0) on a branch inside the DeepCenter-reject path of add_safe_divisions_postlink is byte-identical when off, and a try/except that falls back to 'reject' makes it fail-soft. x138's cell 0 sets SAFE_DIV_SISTER_MAX_UM to 14.0, so the 7-14 um window is consistent with the geometric gate. Train zarrs are local and trainlab.py already records new_forks/tp_forks/fp_forks per arm, so a CPU lab arm is possible. (2) The pre-registered gate is broken by construction. The short-track filter (OUTPUT_MIN_TRACK_LEN 6, KEEP_DIVISION_COMPONENTS 1) runs AFTER the safe divisions. A rejected candidate q has no incoming edge, so if its own track has 2-5 nodes, control drops it, while a rescued fork joins it to the parent's division component and it survives. So 'nodes identical' fails whenever that happens, and the idea changes nodes, not just forks. Rescued proposals also enter the per-frame (0.008) and global (0.004) caps and can displace forks that are accepted now. The same caveat applies to K3b's dummy gate 5. (3) The gate is underpowered. D3 estimated ~3.3% of marginal forks are evaluable, so FP:TP <= 1:1 on SELECTION is decided by about 0-5 events. 'div_J up on both embryos' is nearly unpassable on 44b6, because DeepCenter was trained on 44b6 (few rejects) and the lab holds only 11 divisions there; a flat result fails. (4) Runtime: the DeepCenter veto passes only the candidate point, so the patch must read t-1/t+1/t+2 crops inside the loop. The estimate is 2-10 s/clip x ~100 hidden clips = 3-17 min. That is inside the ~4 h headroom, but it lands BEFORE the 8.0 h DIVINS gate while the K2 worst-case forecast is 7.8 h, so the insertion could be skipped on the last clips. It therefore depends on L2's deadline retune, which needs the user's OK. (5) The schedule only fits narrowly. Dumps arrive ~19:15-22:00 UTC; a realistic lab arm (splitting two touching blobs at 7-9 um before half-max volumes) takes 4-6 h; the verdict lands ~26 Sep 04:00-10:00; patch plus tests take 2 h; the dummy takes 0.7 GPU-h. The earliest submit is S6 (26 Sep ~18:00) or S7 (27 Sep <= 12:00), and it competes with K3b/K4 for the same slots and is mutually exclusive with K3b. The gate must also be committed before tonight's T9 scoring of the dc0.15/0.20 arms, which reveals TP/FP of the same marginal candidates. (6) A slot is unlikely to produce a finals file. With a +0.0005 centre, R4's likely best result is 'F2 candidate', but §f fixes F2 = exp52 by default (a variant only if F1 >= 0.954, time proven comfortable and honest gates). P(lab pass) ~0.2 x P(LB >= +0.002) ~0.1 gives ~0.02 of reaching F1.
fix: Downgrade it to a lab-only diagnostic: no kernel and no LB slot unless the lab result is overwhelming. Before anyone runs `trainlab.py score` on exp60 shards tonight, commit the gate to CONTEXT.md with a timestamp, rewritten as follows. (a) Replace 'nodes identical' with 'node delta is limited to rescued-candidate tracks readmitted by KEEP_DIVISION_COMPONENTS', count those nodes, and require that their GT-matched share is >= 0.5 on SELECTION. (b) Evaluable rescued forks n >= 6 on 6bba SELECTION and the Wilson 80% lower bound of TP/(TP+FP) > 0.4. (c) 6bba CONFIRMATION div_J delta >= +0.002 and 44b6 ALL delta >= -0.0005, not 'up on both embryos'. (d) Also report forks displaced through the frame/global caps. Build the arm as a separate script that exec's a text-patched copy of add_safe_divisions_postlink in the tail namespace, with image evidence from the local train zarr, and leave trainlab.py and its 69 tests untouched. Only if (a)-(d) pass by 26 Sep 10:00 UTC: build the kernel patch (env flag default 0; try/except falls back to reject; hard per-clip time cap, e.g. 20 s, then skip), run a K dummy (flag-off sha256 == parent; flag-on runtime delta <= 0.1 h/100 clips), and use one slot only if the DIVINS gate is retuned (L2) and K3b is not being probed. Otherwise close it.
realistic_gain: Most likely 0 LB. P(the rewritten lab gate passes) ~0.1-0.2. Even then the R4/§f ceiling is usually 'F2 candidate', which loses to the exp52 default, so the expected finals value is ~+0.0001 or less. The concrete value is diagnostic: it measures whether DeepCenter-rejected geometric candidates carry real divisions on 6bba, which also informs K3b. It also exposes the node-change side effect in K3b's own dummy gate 5. Cost: 5-8 h CPU/agent time, 0 GPU if it stays lab-only. If it went to LB: ~0.7 GPU-h dummy, one slot, +3-17 min hidden runtime.
